question:
A 74-year-old male presents to the emergency department with progressive dyspnea over the last
month, now occurring with minimal exertion. His medical history includes poorly controlled diabetes
mellitus, hypertension, end-stage renal disease, and obesity. His medications include insulin,
metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, and ibuprofen, though he is not consistently compliant. He
received dialysis 2 days ago and generally maintains his appointments. His ECG and chest radiograph
are normal. Laboratory findings show: Serum values: - Na+: 135 mEq/L - K+: 4.5 mEq/L - Cl-: 100
mEq/L - HCO3-: 19 mEq/L - BUN: 79 mg/dL - Glucose: 75 mg/dL - Creatinine: 5.5 mg/dL - Ca2+: 9.2
mg/dL - Mg2+: 1.7 mEq/L - AST: 11 U/L - ALT: 11 U/L Complete blood count: - WBC: 4,500/mm^3 -
Platelets: 150,000/mm^3 - Neutrophils: 54% - Lymphocytes: 25% - Monocytes: 3% - Eosinophils: 1% -
Basophils: 1% - Hemoglobin: 8.2 g/dL - Hematocrit: 22% - MCV: 82 µm^3 Vital signs: - Temperature:
99.5°F (37.5°C) - Pulse: 89/min - BP: 144/85 mmHg - Respirations: 10/min - O2 saturation: 97% on
room air What side effect is most commonly associated with the long-term therapy that should be
initiated for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Dialysis-induced hypotension (B) Hypokalemia (C)
Metabolic alkalosis (D) Hyperkalemia (E) Aluminum toxicity (F) Pruritus (G) Iron overload (H)
Hypophosphatemia (I) Hypertension (J) Secondary hyperparathyroidism
 A. Hypertension
B. Metabolic alkalosis
C. Iron overload
D. Hyperkalemia
E. Aluminum toxicity
F. Pruritus
G. Hypokalemia
H. Dialysis-induced hypotension
I. Hypophosphatemia
J. Secondary hyperparathyroidism
